newsitem.title: BURMA: Bomb blast kills four at Burmese Buddhist site.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast kills four at Burmese Buddhist site.

text.p: Two timebombs exploded at a Burmese Buddhist shrine on Christmas night, killing four people and wounding 18, a government spokesman said on Thursday.

The bombs went off on Wednesday at the Kaba Aye and Maha Pasana Cave about four km (2.5 miles) from Rangoon as hordes of pilgrims were paying homage to the Sacred Tooth Relic, which is on loan from China.
A security officer, a Red Cross worker and two members of the government-sponsored Union Solidarity and Development Association (USDA) were killed in the second blast, official media reported.
The Sacred Tooth Relic, believed to be a tooth of the Lord Buddha, was brought to Burma on December 6 on loan for 90 days. It was not damaged, the media reported.
The Chinese Embassy in Rangoon on Thursday denounced the explosions. "We are shocked...and strongly condemn this terrorist action," it said in a statement.

"The Chinese Buddha's Tooth Relic came to Myanmar (Burma) at the request of the Myanmar government and the desire of the great majority of Myanmar Buddhists," it added. "The bomb attacks...blaspheme the Buddha and go against the will of the people."
The spokesman for the military government told Reuters the blasts were being investigated. "We will be able to have a better idea of who did it after the investigation is completed."
Authorities closed public access to the relic. "It may be reopened to the public tomorrow," a Religious Affairs Ministry official said.
Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), which took power in 1988, faced renewed unrest in the past month when students staged two weeks of street protests.
It also faces ethnic guerrilla armies such as the Karen in eastern Burma.

Neighbouring China is one of a handful of countries to maintain close ties to the SLORC, which has been accused by Western nations of widespread human rights abuses, including restrictions on Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

The Christmas blasts were the first reported in or around Rangoon since a bomb went off outside the U.S. Embassy in July. No one was hurt in that explosion, which the SLORC blamed on "destructionists". No group claimed responsibility.
Official media said the bombs were planted by "a group of dastardly destructive elements", aimed at harming Burma-China ties and causing "terror and anxiety among the people".
The movement of the relic, which was to have been displayed in about 12 towns on its way to and back from northern Mandalay, was now uncertain, a government official said.
